text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD - Route53 health-check failures and 5xx spike for api.redwood.example in us-west-3 (usw3). Critical.

sarah: I'm on call, looking at the dashboard. seeing a sharp 503/504 increase from edge -> origin errors.

mike: Confirmed. ELB target group healthy count dropping in usw3b, 5xxs correlate with increased latency from a subset of ENIs.

ashwin: digging into Route53 query logs + edge logs now. early hypothesis: regional cache stale responses + weight routing causing concentrated traffic to a degraded AZ.

jordan: how many customers impacted? is this tiered?

laura: Support: several customers reported timeouts, mainly writes (POSTs) to our ingestion endpoints. Ticket volume up ~3x. No major account-wide outages yet but several 5xx alerts in console.

mike: quick check: ELB 5xx graph: https://grafana.redwood/prod/elbs/usw3/api-elk -> spike at 12:03 UTC. Healthy hosts in target group fell from 18 -> 9 over 2 min.

ashwin: route53 logs sample:
```
2026-03-15T12:02:58Z query: api.redwood.example A from 203.0.113.45 -> response weight=100, cached=true, status=SERVFAIL
2026-03-15T12:03:01Z healthcheck: edge 54.239.x.x failed TTL=60
```
looks like some edge caches are returning SERVFAIL/cached stale entries.

sarah: mitigation options: 1) shift weighted DNS away from usw3 to eu-west-1 as failover 2) increase ELB capacity / drain unhealthy hosts slower 3) enable fallback model in Redwood routing layer. Which first?

mike: do (1) + (3) in parallel. lowering TTL to 30s so changes propagate faster. I'll submit Route53 change.

ashwin: opening AWS support case now, include logs + traceroutes.

mike: applying change:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z2EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-failover","Weight":90,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"54.12.34.56"}]}}]}'
```

mike: submitted. Change ID C9876543210. Waiting for propagation.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support case 543210 opened (severity: high). Assigned to AWS Networking team.

laura: notifying top 10 affected customers via status.redwood and email. Draft in #customer-comms ready to send after confirmation.

jordan: monitoring: 12:08 UTC after weight update -> queries to eu-west-1 increased, overall 5xx rate started trending down. latency also improving for a subset.

ashwin: AWS replied: they saw Route53 edge cache discrepancy for a handful of POPs in the region; they are purging caches and investigating internal routing to edge. ETA unknown.

sarah: handoff: mike takes next 30m for mitigation + communications. I'll follow up at 12:40 UTC for bridge and postmortem notes.

mike: on it. also started ELB scale-up for usw3 to reduce pressure: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --health-check-interval-seconds 10` (temporary).

ashwin: added temporary Route53 TTL change to 15s for the weighted record to speed final convergence.

laura: status page updated: "Partial degradation affecting writes in us-west-3; traffic being shifted to eu-west-1. Investigating." :rotating_light:

customer-success: we have 4 enterprise customers asking for ETA, passing the update. they're ok with failover for now.

aws-support-bot: AWS: "We've escalated to Edge routing team; cache purge in progress for affected POPs. Monitoring propagation. Please provide next hop captures if issues persist."

mike: 12:18 UTC: 5xx rate down ~70% vs peak. still some edge-origin timeouts. Keeping weighted shift in place until AWS confirms full recovery.

sarah: adding this to incidents tracker and will schedule a postmortem. Ops action items:
- collect Route53 change logs/change-IDs
- gather ELB target group health timelines
- collect customer tickets and affected prefixes
- follow up with AWS support case 543210

jordan: thanks team. handoff notes: mike owns mitigation until 12:40 UTC, sarah will drive post-incident review. :thumbsup:

mike: logging final note here before handoff: traffic redirected, AWS purging caches; will watch for any reversion. if regrades happen, plan B is to fail traffic to standby region and open k8s autoscale for ingestion workers.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> mitigated (partial) at 12:25 UTC. Assigning incident ID INC-2026-03-15-01.

laura: sending customer comms now and creating follow-up doc.

sarah: thanks all. closing the live thread; will reopen if new alerts appear. postmortem owners: sarah (lead), ashwin (root cause), mike (mitigation timeline), laura (customer comms).
